correct_answer: No — the CMO's approval was specifically scoped to 'last-season/end-of-life SKUs only' and SUMMER40 applies to current-season mainline; the approval does not cover this promotion
rationale: The CMO's emoji approval in November 2025 was given in response to a specific, scoped request: Tom Nguyen asked for 40% on 'last-season inventory' and Rachel Fong confirmed 'For clearance/last-season only? Not mainline?' before giving the checkmark. Derek Walsh received the same approval under the same conditions. The SUMMER40 promotion applies to 48 current-season mainline SKUs — this is categorically outside the scope of what was approved. Derek's email claim that 'Rachel approved 40% for us' is technically true but materially misleading; the approval was conditioned on product type. Answer B incorrectly treats the emoji as blanket approval without reading the conditional scoping in the thread. Answer C identifies a real procedural issue (no 30-day advance submission) but frames it as the PRIMARY violation — the substantive violation (wrong product category) is more fundamental and would not be cured by timely submission. Answer D tries to split the difference but mischaracterizes the situation; the depth itself was never approved for mainline product, so there is no partial compliance.
